Chapter 12: Rising Strong at Work—Building Resilient Teams and Cultures
If you think the principles of rising strong are just for individuals, think again. These ideas are just as important for our teams, our organizations, and even whole communities.
Have you ever noticed how much a workplace culture can shape how people deal with failure, conflict, or big changes? It's something most of us don’t really see—until we're right in the middle of it.
Picture this: a team’s just faced a major setback. The mood in the room? Tense. You can almost feel the disappointment in the air. But instead of pointing fingers or pretending nothing happened, the team leader does something different. She invites everyone to share their side of the story. As people open up, you can almost see the walls coming down. Folks move from being defensive to actually understanding one another. Turns out, many were struggling quietly, each one thinking they were alone in their fears and frustrations.
So, what does it really take to build a resilient team? It all starts with trust, honesty, and real support. Take the manager who, after a tough quarter, shared her own struggles and invited her team to do the same. The impact? They became more connected, more innovative, and better able to bounce back. Instead of hiding from failure, they learned from it—and grew stronger together.
Too many organizations fall into the trap of punishing mistakes or dodging tough conversations. But here’s something to pay attention to: true resilience comes from honest dialogue, shared vulnerability, and learning together. When we make space for people to be real—to talk about what’s hard and support each other through it—our workplaces become more adaptable, more creative, and just plain stronger.
Think about a teacher, after a challenging year, sharing her experiences with her colleagues. Together, they brainstorm ways to support each other and their students. That single conversation didn’t just change her outlook—it transformed the whole school community.
Rising strong at work isn’t just about getting more done or boosting performance. It’s about building cultures where people feel safe to take risks, to stumble, and to learn. It’s about creating an environment where everyone has the chance to rise strong—side by side.
